headline: Galvis walks it off after Simmons ties it in the ninth
recap: Freddy Galvis led off the bottom of the ninth with a solo home run to right field, giving the Phillies a 6-5 win over the Atlanta Braves. Galvis's blast came one half-inning after Andrelton Simmons hit a two-run homer off Jonathan Papelbon to tie the game 5-5, with Chris Johnson scoring ahead of him.

Kyle Kendrick started for Philadelphia and allowed three earned runs on four hits over six innings, striking out eight and walking three. Atlanta's Alex Wood lasted 4 2/3 innings, giving up four earned runs on nine hits with four strikeouts and three walks.

Carlos Ruiz drove in three runs for the Phillies, with a two-run single in the third scoring Cesar Hernandez and Kevin Frandsen and a run-scoring double in the fifth that brought home Chase Utley. Galvis also singled home Ruiz in the fifth before his game-ending homer. Papelbon was charged with a blown save for the Simmons homer but earned the win when Galvis answered in the bottom of the ninth.
